public: # inputloop
The shop Corwin Brust and Bryant Frankford keep together, with Brigidt (GitHub: definitelynotaspren)
as a lab partner. This folder draws it the way topology wants to: one `TOPOLOGY.md` per thing, in four
kinds of container.
| pillar | what it holds here | folder |
| place | the hosts the work runs and lives on | `hosts/` |
| part | projects, components, files and tools | `projects/` |
| path | how work moves: mirroring, tangling, the atoms round trip | `paths/` |
| person | who answers for what | `people/` |
Four projects are private (`obsmage-corwin`, `about-corwin`, `gitcha`, `c4`). Each says `private: hide`
and keeps what it holds under a `## Private` heading, so the drawing names them and nothing more until
someone chooses to show them. The rule is in `spec/TOPOLOGY-md.md`.
Where a fact is not yet written down, the file says so instead of guessing.
# avalon

Corwin's workstation, and the machine most of the shop's work is started and signed on. The Windows side of the shop (Emacs for Windows builds, MSYS2 shells, the folder the agents land work in) lives here.
The app can draw it as a `server`. It is not reachable from outside; nothing here depends on that changing.
# code.bru.st
Corwin's self-hosted Forgejo, the primary place his projects are published. The canonical copy of a
project lives here; GitHub mirrors it.
# github.com/inputloop
The inputloop organisation on GitHub: the shop's shared home, and where people who work in GitHub terms
can reach what is published. A repository there may be public or private; each says which.
# gw10
The ghostwheel host behind ghostwheel.cloud and the literate façade.
The lab is close to taking on its management.
# gw15
A ghostwheel host named in the shop's host list. What it does is not yet described here; add it when someone writes it down.
# gw19
A ghostwheel host named in the shop's host list. What it does is not yet described here; add it when someone writes it down.
# gw26
The host topology is put on first: Debian 13, answering over HTTPS. The by-hand steps are in
`runcards/RUNCARD-2026-10-31-gw26.md`. Nothing has been run there from this repository yet.
# gw33
The ghostwheel host for the development site dev.ghostwheel.chat, where the `vibrobeast` account works.
# gw4
A small ghostwheel host that mainly runs one thing: Corwin's IRC bouncer (ZNC), with a healer project (`znc-healer`) that grew there.
# gw7
The ghostwheel host Corwin and Bryant share for the garden runtime.
# atoms-roundtrip
An OBS configuration is split into atoms, rolled up into `STAGES.md`, edited by a person or a tool, and
unrolled back. If both sides changed since the pin, the tool stops and names the atoms in conflict.
It never picks a side.
# mirror
How work moves out: everything is mirrored. The self-hosted forge at code.bru.st holds the canonical
copy (first push; merges go through Corwin), and GitHub, under the inputloop org, is where people can
reach it. A project that is private stays private in both places.
# recipe-tangle
`RECIPE.org` is tangled by `sh bin/tangle.sh` into `bin/`, `debian/` and `etc/`; `tests/recipe-check.sh`
says whether the tree still agrees with the recipe. Edit the recipe, then tangle; never edit a tangled file alone.
# bryant
Bryant Frankford. Made TopoForge and quantum3d5.
# corwin
Corwin Brust, `corwin@bru.st`. Commits are authored as him, unsigned; signing is his act, by hand.
The agent's part in a commit is a byline on its last line.
# definitelynotaspren
Credited by this GitHub handle. A lab partner in inputloop since 2026-10-25; NextTime-Dev is her work.
# NextTime-Dev
Community time banking for Nextcloud: post a request, volunteer, earn hours. An hour of help is worth
an hour whoever gives it. An admin, or a three-vote community process, approves hours, and every
movement of hours lands in a public ledger. It is Brigidt's work (GitHub: definitelynotaspren), tested
on seven Nextcloud versions as of 2026-10-29. A browser demo is in `demo/index.html`.

public: # obsmage
OBS Studio kept as a living, literate configuration, with plugins that sense the room. A downstream
build of OBS whose whole configuration is split into key/value atoms that a person or a tool can read,
diff, version and change, with credentials kept out of everything published.
## Parts
- `omg-atoms` splits an OBS configuration into atoms and joins it back (INI byte-exact, JSON parse-equal).
- `omg-compose` audits and rebinds multi-monitor captures by stable id.
- `omg-heal` plans, builds and heals Debian and source builds.
- `obsmage-core` is the plugin skeleton (designed, not built).
## Files that say what it is
| file | says |
| `README.md` | what works today, what is only designed, how to try it |
| `CONVENTIONS.md` | atoms and their classes, the `STAGES.md` seam, why nothing is reorganized automatically |
| `MODEL.md` | the direction, for a brand-new reader |
| `STAGES.md` | the one-file roll-up of every atom (two readers, two writers, a pin) |
| `AGENTS.md` | who commits, and what must be green before a push |
| `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md` | the requirements R1 to R8 and where each stands |
Personal recipes live in their own repositories that consume this one; `obsmage-corwin` is the first.
# obsmage-core
The core plugin skeleton: where AR desktop control and camera calibration will attach
(`docs/AR-CONTROL.md`). Designed, not built.
# omg-atoms
`tools/omg_atoms.py`: `find`, `verify`, `split`, `join`, `rollup`, `unroll` over an OBS configuration.
Secret atoms go to a local vault (mode 600) and appear in anything published only as `@secret(len=N)`.
Tests: `tests/test_atoms.py`, `tests/e2e.sh` with `--prove-red`.
# omg-compose
`tools/omg_compose.py`: audits which captures bind to a display by index (fragile) or by stable id,
rebinds them, keeps screen-map scenes current. Never deletes; hides and reports. Every write is behind
`--write` and leaves a dated backup. See `docs/COMPOSER.md`. Tests: `tests/test_compose.py`.
# omg-heal
`packaging/healer/omg-heal`: the build healer. Follows `main` (the default), project meta, tags, or
signed tags only. Test: `tests/e2e-healer.sh`.
# obsmage-corwin
A personal recipe repository that consumes `obsmage`. It is private: this page says only that it exists.
private: One person's OBS rig, as recipe and atoms: `RECIPE.md`, `SCENES.md`, `STAGES.md`, `atoms/`, `journal/`,
and `hosts/avalon` and `hosts/giza` (the giza port is parked). Credentials are `secret` atoms and never
appear in the tree. Read `CONVENTIONS.md` of obsmage and `RECIPE.md` here before changing how things are kept.

public: # quantum3d5
A 3D particle, atom and molecule simulator for learning chemistry and physics in the browser, offline.
Bryant's. Needs a browser and nothing else: no account, no server, 0 network connections as of
2026-10-29. A Realism page says which parts are real physics, simplified, or faked.

public: # topology
Draw what you have, from the files that describe it. Reads `TOPOLOGY.md` from the git repositories you
keep, sorts what they say by place, part, path and person, and draws it with TopoForge.
## Files that say what it is
| file | says |
| `README.org` | what it is, how to try it, where things are |
| `RECIPE.org` | the source of `bin/`, `debian/` and `etc/`; tangle it to rebuild them |
| `spec/TOPOLOGY-md.md` | the file format and the show-private rule |
| `taxonomy/pillars.json` | the four pillars, two axes, six tensions, as data |
| `AGENTS.md` | who commits and where work lands |
| `examples/inputloop/` | this drawing of the shop |
Private parts of any `TOPOLOGY.md` stay hidden until the component or the person says show.
# topology-command
`perl/Topology/script/topology`: reads `repos.d`, fetches the repositories listed, builds the graph as
small files (`r/` and `c/`, written twice) and serves it read-only. Modules: `Config`, `Doc`, `Repo`,
`Graph`, `Taxonomy`, `Build`, `CSV`, `Server`. Every feature can be switched off in
`/etc/topology/topology.conf`; `ceiling = spa` leaves only the app's files.
# topology-www
`www/`: the front door (`index.html`), the app (`app.html`), the stylesheets (`css/topology.css`, with
egad's tokens in `css/egad.css`) and TopoForge. Works with no server (Zero Sharing). Checked for
accessibility by `tests/a11y-check.mjs`.
# topoforge
TopoForge, the single-file network and diagram designer Bryant Frankford made. It is kept in this
repository unchanged; improvements to it belong in Bryant's own copy first.
# topology-core
`www/js/topology-core.js`: the rules, not the pictures: reading `TOPOLOGY.md`, deciding what private parts
show, the settings kept in the browser, and the CSV TopoForge opens. The same rules are written a second
time in Perl (`Topology::Doc`), and both run against `spec/fixtures/`.
# vibrobeast
A memory Claude keeps on your own computer in plain files, with the skills, persona sheets and shared
rooms built around it. Ships as a plugin carrying three stdio MCP servers, and works as a plugin
marketplace for people who add the repository. Its skills are kept in their own repository,
`vibrobeast-skills`, so a person can take the skills without the servers.
A commit to vibrobeast is not complete unless its shelf on inputloop is correct.
# vibrobeast-skills
Written ways of working that Claude reads when a task calls for them; each skill is also a slash
command. 78 skills, counted 2026-10-30. Installs into Claude Desktop or Claude Code as a plugin. Each
skill says when it applies, what it does, how it can fail and how to switch it off; several carry
checks that are shown able to fail before anyone trusts them.
